assessment_summary: I reviewed the guide and summary, then inspected the resulting environment and ran behavioral checks. Toolchain locations were verified (/opt/flutter, /opt/android-sdk, JDK 17) and versions exactly match the guide: Flutter 3.35.7, Dart 3.9.2, Java 17, configured via flutter config (android-sdk, jdk-dir) and /etc/profile.d/flutter.sh. flutter doctor -v passes Flutter, Android toolchain (SDK 35.0.0, licenses accepted), Linux toolchain, device, and network; only Chrome and Android Studio are missing, both inapplicable/headless-GUI limitations. Dependencies resolve (pub get --offline: 'Got dependencies!', 266 packages) and flutter analyze reports 0 errors (96 info lints). The decisive check was re-building the flavor APK: flutter build apk --debug --flavor ni ... completed successfully (exit 0), and the artifact was validated with unzip -t (no errors), sha1sum matching the recorded .sha1, and apkanalyzer reporting package wemove.app.bipu version 2.8.0 with a proper launcher activity and ni-flavor assets — confirming the app compiles and packages correctly. The final method (direct Flutter tarball rather than the guide's recommended-not-required fvm) still achieves the exact required versions, so it is not a deviation. Limitations: no Android emulator/AVD was installed and no physical device is attached, so I could not observe the app's runtime UI on a device; the repo has no test/ directory so no test suite could run; Android Studio (GUI) and Chrome/Xcode are unavailable, consistent with a headless Linux container and not required to build or run the Android app. These limitations concern optional GUI/runtime-observation tooling rather than the installation itself. Overall the installation is complete and the software builds and packages successfully, supporting a success outcome.
